translations.text: Love righteousness, you judges of the earth. Think about the Lord with good thoughts, and seek him with a sincere heart.
For he is found by those who do not put him to the test, and he reveals himself to those who trust in him.
For evil thoughts lead away from God, but the power that tests rebukes fools.
For wisdom does not enter a soul entangled in evil, nor does she dwell in a body enslaved to sin.
For the holy spirit and discipline flee from deceit, withdraw from the thoughts of those who lack knowledge, and rebuke every injustice that comes.

For the spirit of wisdom loves humanity, but she does not acquit a blasphemous people of what their lips say. For God witnesses their innermost thoughts, truly examines the heart, and hears the human tongue.
For the spirit of the Lord has filled the world, and the one who holds everything together knows its voice.
Therefore no one who speaks unjustly remains hidden, nor will that person escape a judgment of condemnation.
For an inquiry will be made into the thoughts of the wicked, and the report of their words will come before the Lord to convict them of their wickedness.
For the jealous ear hears everything, and the whisper of grumbling is not hidden.
Therefore beware of useless grumbling, and keep your tongues from slander. For secret speech does not pass without consequence, and a lying mouth kills the soul.
Do not long for death through the errors of your life, and do not entangle yourselves in ruinous destruction through the work of your hands.
For God did not make death, nor does he desire the destruction of the living.
Rather, he created everything to exist, and there is life in what the world brings forth. There is no deadly poison in them, and Sheol has no dominion over the earth.
For righteousness is immortal.
But the wicked called him by their words and deeds. They considered him their friend, wasted away, swore an oath, and made a covenant with him, because they were worthy to belong to him.
For they said to themselves, without thinking rightly, “Our life is short and full of distress. There is no remedy when a person departs, and no one has appeared who has been released from Sheol.
For we came into being suddenly, and afterward we return to being as though we had never existed. For the breath in our nostrils is like smoke, and speech stirs like a spark in our hearts.
When it is extinguished, the body becomes like ashes, and the spirit disperses like thin air.
Our name is forgotten in time, and no one remembers our deeds. Our life passes like the traces of clouds, and like mist driven away by the sun’s rays, with the sun’s heat bearing down upon it.
For our life is a passing shadow, and there is no remedy at our departure, because it has been sealed, and no one can reverse it.
Come, then, let us enjoy these good things, and eagerly make use of these created things while we are young.
Let us fill ourselves with choice wine and perfumes, and let the [?] of the air not pass us by.
Let us crown ourselves with rose blossoms before they wither.
Let none of us go without pleasure, even into our old age, and let us leave traces of our enjoyment everywhere. For this is our portion, and this is our inheritance.
Let us overpower the righteous poor person. Let us have no pity on the widow or the orphan, and let us show no respect for an old man advanced in years.”
Let our strength be our law of righteousness, because the weak are condemned as feeble.
Let us harass the righteous man, because he is not pleasing to us. He opposes our deeds, reproaches us over the works of the law, and reminds us of the offenses committed in our arrogance.
He claims to have knowledge of God and says of himself, “I am God’s son.”
He has become a reproach to our thoughts; even seeing him is a burden to us.
For his way of life is unlike other people’s, and his paths are different.
He considers us unclean and keeps away from our ways as though from uncleanness. He calls the paths and the final end of the righteous blessed, and boasts that God is his Father.
Let us see whether his words are true; let us test him at his departure.
For if the righteous man is God’s son, God will accept him and rescue him from the hands of those who have risen against him.
Let us interrogate him with humiliation and torture, so that we may learn how carefully he maintains his humility and test whether there is evil in him.
Let us condemn him to a disgraceful death, for, according to his words, there will be an inquiry concerning him.
The foolish thought these things and went astray, because their wickedness blinded them.
They did not know God’s mysteries, did not hope for the reward of holiness, and did not value the souls of blameless elders.
For God created humanity to be free from decay; humanity was formed in the image of his likeness.
Through the devil’s envy, death entered the world, and those who belong to him experience it.
But the souls of the righteous are in God’s hands, and torment does not come near them.
In the eyes of fools they seemed to be dead, and their departure was considered a misfortune.
Their departure from us was regarded as destruction, but they are at peace.
For even if they are condemned in the eyes of human beings, their hope is full of life.
He tested them a little, and they were disciplined a little, but they will inherit much, because God tested them and found them worthy of him.
He tested them like gold in a furnace and accepted them like burnt offerings and sacrifices of well-being.
In due time their examination will take place, and the righteous will run among the wicked like sparks among reeds.
The peoples will rejoice, the nations will be glad, and the Lord will reign over them forever.
Those who trust in him understand the truth, and those who are faithful wait for him in love, because he gives grace and mercy to his chosen ones, and his care is over his holy ones.
But the wicked will receive disgrace in keeping with their thoughts—those who despised the Lord and withdrew from his righteous ones.
For whoever rejects wisdom and discipline is miserable, and his hope is empty. Their toil has no understanding in it, and their deeds do not prosper.
Their wives are unwise, their children are wicked, and their offspring are cursed.
For it is well with the barren woman who has not been defiled, who has not known an adulterous bed. She will receive fruit when souls are examined.

And the eunuch whose hands have committed no violation of the law, and who has conceived no evil against the Lord, will be given, because of his goodness and faithfulness, a special favor and a desirable inheritance in the Lord’s house.
There is a choice reward for good toil, and the roots of chastity will not be uprooted.
The children of adulterers will not reach maturity, and offspring from an unlawful bed will be destroyed.
Even if they live long, they will be counted as nothing, and their old age will end in dishonor.
If they die prematurely, they have no hope and no comfort on the appointed day.
For the offspring of the wicked have a bitter end.
It is better to be childless with honor, for there is life in the remembrance of honor, because it is known to God and to human beings.

When it is present, people imitate it, and when it has departed, they long for it. In this world it wears an ornament and a crown, and it is shown to have won the contest of those who are without blemish.
But the numerous offspring of the wicked are of no use. Those who come from foreign seed will not put down deep roots and have no firm foundation.
Even if they put out shoots and branches, they will flourish only for a time and will not stand securely. They will be shaken by the wind and uprooted by a powerful wind.
Their branches will finally be broken, and their fruit will be spoiled, unfit to eat and good for nothing.
Children born from an unlawful bed are witnesses against their parents when they are called to account.
But even if the righteous person dies prematurely, he will be at rest; and if he dies after a long life, he will be found in honor.
Old age and honor do not come from a long span of time, nor are they measured by the number of years.
Rather, a person's understanding is his gray hair, and a peaceful life is the full stature of old age.
Because he pleased God, he was loved; because he was living among sinners, God removed him.
He was snatched away so that evil would not change his thinking and deceit would not lead his tongue astray.
For evil zeal ruins good things, and the turmoil of desire corrupts a good mind.
Having been perfected in a short time, he fulfilled a long span of time.

For his soul pleased God, and because he was upright, God quickly lifted him out of the midst of evil. But the peoples saw this and did not understand, nor did they consider why he judged him this way.
God's grace and mercy are among his holy ones, and God's care is over his chosen ones.
He judges the righteous and destroys the wicked while they are alive. Young people who depart after a short time are better than the long lives of dishonest elders.
For they will see the death of the righteous person and will not understand what God planned for him or why the Lord took care of him.
They will see him and despise him, but the Lord himself will laugh at them.

After these things they will become a dishonorable ruin and an everlasting disgrace among the dead. For saws will cut them apart without a sound, and they will be shaken from their foundations. They will be utterly laid waste and brought to ruin, and their memory will perish.
Deceit will enter their thoughts about their foolish deeds, and their waywardness will rebuke them openly, before their eyes.
Then the righteous person will stand with great boldness before those who oppressed him and those who cheated him of the fruit of his toil.
For they will see him and be seized with great fear, and they will be astonished when they see his glory.

They will say to themselves in remorse, and in the anguish of their spirits they will groan and say, “This is the man whom we once made a laughingstock, an object of reproach, and a byword among fools.
We considered his life foolish and his death disgraceful.
How has he been counted among the children of God, and how is his inheritance among the holy ones?
So we were wandering away from the way of truth. The light of righteousness did not shine on us, and the sun did not rise for us.
Our paths were filled with our sins and destruction. We walked through an untrodden wilderness, and we did not know the way of the Lord.
What benefit did our arrogance bring us? Or what did our arrogant way of life gain us?
It passed like a shadow. And what benefit did our arrogant way of life bring us? All these things passed like shadows and like news that travels swiftly.
And like a ship passing over the waves of the sea: once it has passed, its tracks cannot be recognized, nor its course among the paths of the waves.

Or like a bird flying through the air, whose track cannot be traced: it beats its wings, stirs and cleaves the light wind, splits the air with the strength of its pinions, and moves along with the beating of its wings. Afterward its passage cannot be discerned, and no one can find a sign of its path.
Or like an arrow shot at a target, which pierces the air, and immediately the air returns to its place, so that its path cannot be discerned.
So we too were born and came to an end. We could show no sign of goodness, but were overwhelmed by our wicked deeds.”

For the hope of the wicked is like sand carried off by the wind, like chaff swept away by a whirlwind, like smoke scattered by the wind, and like the memory of a traveler's day. So we have passed away.
But the righteous live forever. Their reward is with the Lord, and their thoughts are with the Most High.
Therefore they will receive a glorious kingdom and a crown of beauty from the Lord's hand. With his right hand he shelters them, and with his arm he shields them.
For their sake, in his zeal, he will arm everything, and he will arm all his creation alongside him for war against his enemies.
He will put on righteousness as a breastplate and place on his head a helmet of judgment without falsehood.
He will take holiness as an invincible shield.
He will sharpen the sword of his anger wondrously, and the people of the world will wage war alongside him against fools.
Arrows of flashing light and lightning will pass over them, and they will be loosed as at a target from the curved bow of the clouds.
In fury he will hurl hailstones upon them like rocks. The waters of the sea will rage against them, and rivers will violently drown them.
A terrifying wind will rise against them and scatter them like a whirlwind. It will devastate the whole land of the wicked and crush the dominion and thrones of the mighty who practice injustice.
Listen, therefore, you kings, and understand; learn, you judges of the ends of the earth.
Pay attention, you who rule over many and boast of the multitudes of nations.
For your dominion was given by the Lord, and your power comes from the Most High. He examines your deeds and searches your thoughts.
For you were servants of his kingdom, but you did not judge rightly, did not keep his law, and did not walk according to God's purposes.
He will rise against you terribly and swiftly, for a terrible judgment will come upon those in high positions.
For a humble king is close to mercy, but the powerful will be called to account powerfully.
For the Lord of all shows no partiality and is not intimidated by greatness, because he made both the great and the small, and he cares for everyone equally.
And he examines the mighty in truth.
My words are addressed to you, rulers, so that you may learn wisdom and not fall.
For those who love holiness will be made holy in holiness, and those who learn it will find beauty.
Therefore desire my words and love them, and you will be instructed.
Wisdom is radiant and does not decay. She is easily seen by those who love her and is revealed to those who seek her.
And she reveals herself to those who long to seek her.
Whoever comes to her early will not grow weary, for he will readily find her standing at his door.
For thinking about her is perfect wisdom, and those who keep watch for her will soon be free from worry.
For she herself comes and visits those who are worthy of her. She appears to them on their paths, and she is constant, meeting them in all their thoughts.
For the beginning of desire for her is truth and instruction.
Concern for instruction is love; love is the keeping of her law, and understanding her law is truth that does not decay.
And deeds free from corruption bring people near to God.
For desire for wisdom leads up to kingship.
If you desire thrones and royal scepters, rulers of the people, honor wisdom so that you may reign forever.
I will tell what wisdom is and how she came to be, and I will not hide mysteries from you. I will trace her from before creation, openly set forth knowledge of her, and not depart from what is right.
And I will not walk in envy, because it has no fellowship with wisdom.
A multitude of wise people is the life of the world, and a wise king sustains the people.
Therefore be instructed by my words, and you will inherit life.
For I too am a mortal human being, like everyone else, a descendant of the first man, who was born of the earth. In my mother's womb I was formed into flesh.
For a period of ten months I took shape in blood, from a man's seed and from the desire of sleeping together.
When I was born, I entered the air shared by all, and like everyone else I fell upon the earth. My first sound, like everyone else's, was to begin crying.
And I was carefully wrapped in swaddling clothes.
For no king or ruler has ever had a different kind of birth.
For everyone has one entrance into the world, and likewise one departure.
Because of this I prayed, and a spirit of wisdom was given to me. I called out, and a spirit of knowledge came to me.
I desired her more than scepters and thrones, and I did not consider wealth comparable to her.
Nor did I compare her to a precious stone, because all gold before her is like a little dust, and silver is regarded as mud before her.
I loved her more than beauty and health. I chose her over light, because wisdom’s own light never sleeps.
All good things came to me together with her, and immeasurable wealth was in her hands.
I delighted in all these things because wisdom guides them, though I did not know that she came before them all.
I learned without deceit, and I give without envy; I will not hide her wealth from you.
For she is an inexhaustible treasure for human beings. Those who acquired her entered into friendship with God, because they stood firm in freely given instruction.
May God grant me to speak with good judgment and also to think rightly about what is said, because he is wisdom’s guide, and he sets the wise straight.
In his hand are we and our words, all wisdom and knowledge and deeds.
For he gave me knowledge free from falsehood, to understand how the world is constituted and how the elements work.
The beginning, end, and middle of times, the changes of things, and how times pass;
The course of the years and the arrangement of the stars.
The nature of domestic animals and the fury of wild beasts, the force of the winds and the thoughts of human beings, the varieties of plants and the powers of roots.
I learned everything hidden and everything revealed.

For wisdom, who is skilled in everything, taught me. In her is a spirit of knowledge, holy, unique, subtle, having many parts, moving freely, clear in speech, unstained, wise and steadfast, unyielding, loving good things, wise, not deceived, and beneficial;
Loving humanity, strong, steadfast, free from anxiety, powerful and able to do everything, attending to everything, intelligent, pure, embracing all spirits, subtle and radiant.
Wisdom moves and acts in every movement; she is the one who holds sway above [?] because of her purity.
She is a breath of God’s power and stands in the glory of God, who rules all. She is without falsehood; therefore nothing defiled enters her.
Wisdom is the radiance of light and does not perish. She is a mirror of glory for all God’s works and an image of his goodness.
She is one and can do everything. She remains, and everything is renewed in her. In every generation she brings peace to the souls of the devout; she forms friends of God and prophets.
For God loves only those in whom wisdom dwells.
For she is more beautiful than the sun and surpasses the whole arrangement of the stars. I compared her with light, and she was found to surpass it.
After it comes night, but evil does not rule over wisdom.
For she extends herself firmly from end to end and deals gently with everything.
I loved her and sought her from my youth. I sought to make her my bride, because I longed for her beauty.
There is joy and praise of God in companionship with her, because God is her Father, and the Lord of all loves her.
For she is God’s confidante, his partner in counsel, and the glory of all his works.
If wealth is desirable among the world’s possessions, what is richer than wisdom, who made everything?
If someone seeks skill for his work, who is more skilled than she?
If anyone loves righteousness, it is wonderful in her company, for wisdom teaches self-control, righteousness, and courage. Nothing in the world is better for human beings than she is.

If anyone wishes to know much, she knows the things of the past and reveals the things to come. She knows the turns of speech and the beginnings of hidden things. She knows signs and wonders beforehand, and the outcome of times and seasons.
I chose her as my companion, knowing that she would counsel me in good things and take worry and distress away from me.
She brought me praise among many peoples and honor from elders in my youth.
She made me discerning in judgments and admired in the presence of powerful men.
When I am silent, they wait for me; when I open my mouth, they look at me; and when I speak at length, they put their hands over their mouths.
Because of her I will not die, and I will leave an everlasting remembrance to those who come after me.
I will govern peoples, and nations will be subject to me.
Tyrants will hear and be afraid, and they will be sternly disciplined. Among the multitudes I appear good, and in battles I am courageous.
When I enter my house, I rest with wisdom, for there is no bitterness in her dealings and no harm in her companionship, but pleasure and joy.
I considered these things within myself and reflected in my heart that there is life in intimacy with wisdom,

and good pleasure in loving her, inexhaustible wealth in the labor of her hands, knowledge and excellence in studying her words, and unfailing truth in sharing her thoughts. I went about seeking to take her for myself.
I was a bright child, and I received a good soul.
Because of my goodness, I entered an undefiled body.

But I knew that I could not master myself unless God granted it to me—and this is understanding: to know from whom the gift comes. I asked the Lord and pleaded with him, and with all my heart I said to him:
God of my ancestors and Lord of mercies, you made everything by your word,
and by your wisdom you formed humankind to have dominion over the creatures you made,
to govern the creation of the world in truth and righteousness, and to administer judgment with an upright soul.
Give me wisdom from before your throne, and do not reject me from among your servants.
For I am your servant, I am your servant and the son of your maidservant, a weak man, short-lived and lacking understanding of judgment and law.
For even if someone is perfect among human beings, when the spirit that comes from you departs from him, he is counted as nothing.
You are the one who chose me as king to rule your people and as judge over your sons and daughters.
You told me to build a temple on your holy mountain and an altar in the city where you dwell, a likeness of your holy tabernacle, which you prepared long ago.
With you is wisdom, who knows your works. She was with you when you made the worlds, and she knows what is pleasing in your eyes and what is right according to your commandments.
Send her from your holy heavens, and send her from the throne of your majesty, so that she may come and labor with me, and I may know what is pleasing to you.
For she knows and understands everything. She will guide me wisely in all my deeds and guard me by her glory.
Then all my deeds will be acceptable, and I will be worthy of my father's throne.
For what human being knows God's counsel? Or who can work out what the Lord wills?
For the thoughts of mortals are weak, and their plans are uncertain.
For the perishable body weighs heavily on the soul.
Look, we barely comprehend the things on earth. We discover what is before our eyes with difficulty, and we discover what is in our hands with toil. But who can investigate the things in heaven?
Who has known your counsel unless you gave wisdom and sent your Holy Spirit from your heavens?
In this way the paths on earth were made straight, human beings learned your will, and they lived through your wisdom.
She is the one who protected the first father, who was created alone in the world, and rescued him from his own fall.
She gave him strength to rule over everything.
But Cain the wrongdoer turned away from her, and anger destroyed him for killing his brother.
When the flood came upon the earth, Wisdom again saved life: she guided righteous Noah in a vessel of hewn wood.
When the peoples agreed together in evil and were scattered, she recognized the righteous man and kept him blameless before God. She steadfastly protected Abraham in the matter of his beloved son.
When the wicked perished, she rescued righteous Lot, who fled as fire came down upon the five cities.
The evidence of their wickedness remains to this day: they smoke and lie barren, the trees within them bear no fruit, and the person who did not believe stood as a pillar of salt.

For they transgressed against Wisdom and were not gathered in, not only because they did not do good, but because they left a memorial of their folly in the world, so that their wicked deeds could not be forgotten.
But wisdom rescues those who serve her from suffering.

She rescued righteous Jacob when he fled from the anger of his unjust brother. She guided him along straight paths, showed him the kingdom of God, and gave him knowledge of the truth. She increased the fruits of his labor and made him wealthy through his work.
She stood by him against the oppression of his oppressors and made him wealthy.

She protected him from his enemies and strengthened him against those who rose against him. She gave him victory in a mighty struggle, so that he would know that the fear of God is stronger than everything.
She did not abandon righteous Joseph when he was sold, but rescued him from sin.

She went down with him into the pit and did not abandon him in prison, until she gave him a royal scepter and authority over those who had sought to overpower him. She showed that those who accused him were liars and gave him everlasting glory.
She rescued a devout people and delivered a blameless race from the people who oppressed them.
She entered the soul of the Lord's servant, and he stood against fearsome kings with signs and wonders.
She gave the holy ones the reward for their labor and guided them through a wondrous land. She became a shelter for them by day and took the place of starlight by night.
She guided them through the fearsome Red Sea and led them through mighty waters.
The waters covered their enemies, and you brought them up from the depths of the abyss.
Therefore the righteous afflicted the wicked and praised your holy name, Lord, with one voice, and together they praised your mighty hand.
For wisdom opened the mouths of the mute and made the tongues of infants speak clearly.
You directed their deeds through the holy prophet.
They traveled through an uninhabited wilderness and pitched their tents where no path had been made.
They stood firm in battle and struck their enemies.
Your people grew thirsty and called to you, and you gave them water from flinty rock, and relief for their thirst from solid stone.
For when they took vengeance on their enemies, they themselves were in need, and they were given what they needed.
Instead of the source of a river overflowing with blood, with red waters,
as retribution for the children who were killed by command, you gave them water with good, unending life.
Therefore you showed that it was through thirst that you exacted retribution from their adversaries.
When they were tested, and you mercifully disciplined and guided them, they learned that the wicked are scourged and humiliated in anger.
These, Father, you chose, comforted, and tested; but those you killed and condemned like an angry king.
You crushed those far away and those nearby.
Double distress seized them, along with groans at the memory of what had happened.
For they heard of their own retribution, because when things went well for them they did not acknowledge the Lord.
Instead, they mocked what had happened to them, and at the outcome of their departure they were astonished. Their cry was not like that of the righteous.

But their wrongdoing matched their senseless thoughts. Because they went astray and worshiped crawling creatures and animals that cannot speak, you sent many speechless animals against them to humiliate and punish them.
This was so that they would know that a person is judged and punished through the very thing by which he sins.
For you did not lack the power by which you created the world from unformed matter. You could have sent many wolves against them,
or the fury of lions, or terrifying flashes of lightning, or the fury of many unknown animals, or fire that blows and consumes, or the force of fuming smoke, or the force of lightning flashes.
These could not only destroy them; even the sight of them could destroy them.

Apart from all these things, you could have swept them away and destroyed them with a single breath. They could have been pursued by your retribution, and you could have scattered them before the blast of your breath. But you brought everything upon them in measured quantity, in order, and by weight.
For great things always stand before you, and who can stand against your right arm?
For the whole created world is like the blink of an eye before you, and like the dew that descends upon the earth in the morning.
You have mercy on everyone, because you can accomplish everything, and you overlook people's sins when they repent.
You love everything and despise nothing that you have made, for if you had hated anything, you would not have made it.
For how could anything have existed unless you had willed it? Or how could anything have been preserved unless you had commanded it?
You spare everything, because everything belongs to you, Lord; you are the lover of souls.
For your good spirit dwells in everything.
You rebuke those who stumble little by little. You admonish and reprove them for their offenses, so that they may flee from evil and believe in you, Lord.
For even those who formerly lived in the holy land—
You hated them because of their filthy deeds, their acts of sorcery, and their improper rites.
They killed their children without pity. They ate flesh, human wombs. Among themselves they made an image of destruction; in their midst they performed unlawful mysteries.
There was no help for the lives of their people's children, and you wanted to destroy them by the hand of the fathers.
So that God's servants might receive a peaceful dwelling—the land you gave in honor and glory.
Yet you spared even these as human beings. You sent hornets ahead into battle, so that little by little they might destroy them.
But it was not because the wicked were stronger than the righteous that they would destroy them, or that they would be crushed by vicious beasts or by a deadly utterance from the mouth.

But you judged them little by little and gave them an opportunity to repent, because you know that their origin is evil, that their wickedness is planted within them, and that their thoughts never change.
For the offspring of sinners is cursed before the Lord. It was not because you feared sinners that you gave them more time.

For who can say to you, “What are you doing?” Or who can oppose your judgments? Or who can complain about the people of the nations when you destroy them? Or who will stand before you as an avenger on behalf of wicked people?
For there is no other God besides you. You care for everything, and you have shown that you have judged nothing unjustly.
Neither a king nor a ruler can stand before you concerning what you have justly condemned.
You govern everything justly; and whatever ought to be condemned to punishment [?] as foreign to your power.
For your power is the source of justice. You have authority over everything, and you spare everything.
You displayed mighty deeds, yet they did not believe in perfect power alone [?]. You sternly rebuke those whom you know.
You, Lord, have authority over power, and you judge with care. You govern us with complete compassion, for whenever you wish, abundant power is available.
Through these deeds you taught your people and your children that a righteous person ought to love other human beings. You gave your children good hope, and you grant repentance for offenses.
Even the enemies of your servants you condemned to death and humiliated with every punishment; yet, delaying [?], you give them time for supplication, so that they may flee from evil.
With great care you judged your people and your children, those with whose fathers you made covenants, oaths, and good promises.

You carried out judgment for us by scourging those who hate us with tens of thousands of lashes, so that when we judge, we may remember your goodness, and when we are judged, we may look for your mercy.
For when they lived as fools and came to an end unjustly, you punished them through their uncleanness.

For they fled and wandered along the paths of their error, trusting in animals and in what their enemies despised, believing them to be gods—a childish recompense [?] for the foolishness of their deceit.
Therefore, as though they were children without understanding, you sent upon them a judgment that made them a laughingstock.
Those who do not learn from a judgment that makes them a laughingstock will taste God's judgment in earnest.

For they became angry at the very things through which they suffered, because they trusted in them as gods, yet through these very things they would be punished. Those who had previously seen and denied, refusing to seek God in truth, will face the judgment prepared for them.
Vain are the people who do not know God. Even from the good things that are visible, they could not understand the one who exists. They did not examine the works or recognize their maker.
Instead, they regarded fire, wind, the light air, the revolutions of the stars, the flowing waters, the lights of heaven, or the ordering of the world as gods.
If you consider them gods because of their beauty, how much better than they is the one who made them! The one who created beauty is the one who made all these things.
If they feared them because of their power and their wondrous nature, let them learn from these things that the one who made them is better than they are.
For they were created from the greatness of his beauty; the one who created them is plainly seen.
Only slight wrath will come upon these people, because perhaps they went astray while seeking God and trying to find knowledge.
They occupied themselves with his works, becoming corrupted as they investigated them, and were persuaded by outward appearances, because what is seen is beautiful.
Yet he will not let them off at the judgment.
If they were able to know all these things, and discovered and understood the structure of the world, how did they not recognize and find the Lord of the whole creation?

Wretched are those whose hope is in dead things, who call the work of human hands gods: gold and silver, products of craftsmanship, images of animals, and a worthless stone fashioned by hand and set upright.

Or consider wood from the forest: a carpenter eagerly cuts down a standing tree that can be moved easily and skillfully carves it all around. He makes it firm and carves it, fashioning it soundly into a fine object for everyday use.
He uses its shavings to prepare food and eats his fill, supplying from it whatever he lacks.

What is discarded from it is good for nothing, and out of his own imagination he makes an object suited to uncleanness. It is a hard tree, planted beside the water and standing there. He takes it and diligently works on it, and on a day when he is free from work he sketches it and shapes it into a human image.
Or he made it resemble a beautiful animal, coated it with pigments, painted it with red ocher, and adorned it with all the beauty on earth.
He makes a place suited to it, sets it in the wall, and secures it with nails.
He takes care that it stands and does not fall, because he knows that it has no ability to help itself: it is an image and needs someone to help it.
People pray to it about possessions, feasts, and children. A man is not ashamed to speak with something that has no life in it, asking a sick thing to make him well and heal him.
For life, he asks a dead thing to give him life. He pleads with something that does not know how to do him good, and asks something that cannot walk to make his paths straight.
In matters of trade in things made by hand, he makes requests of something that is useless.
Or when he sets out to sail in a ship on the sea, over its astonishing waves, he prays and asks a fragile piece of wood, more fragile than the ship carrying him, to help him.
The ship was made for trade; a craftsman made it with his wisdom.
But you, Father, created everything through your wisdom and care, and provided a way through the sea and secure paths over the waves,
to show that you can preserve life and rescue from anything, and that everything can be done with skill.

Because you yourself willed and made everything, and your wisdom does not cease its work, you therefore allowed human beings to entrust their lives to a small piece of wood, cross mighty waves, and survive.

For from the beginning the chosen giants, who hoped to settle in the world, perished and passed away. They fled and left the world no offspring to reproduce. This ordering of things, which you created, is yours.
Blessed is the wood through which a righteous person is seen.
But what is made by human hands is cursed, both it and its maker, who made a perishable object and called it a god.
The wicked person and his wickedness are hateful to God.
The work and its maker will be condemned together.

For this reason punishment will also come upon the idols of the nations, because they are part of God’s creation, but people made them into an abomination, a stumbling block for human souls, and traps for the feet of foolish people.
For the devising of idols is the beginning of sexual immorality, and they bring destruction to the living.
They did not exist from the beginning, nor will they remain forever.
For human gluttony entered the world; therefore the end came suddenly.

For a father took an offering of mourning amid the trembling of living creatures, and his son too would be taken away [?]. He made an image of a person who was then dead, and now made him the likeness of a god. He gave those under his authority secret rites of worship.
Wickedness spread and grew strong with [?] time, and he observed the teaching like a law. At the command of tyrants, they worshiped carved images.

Because they could not honor in person a man who lived far away, they made themselves an image of those who lived far away, a recognizable image to honor the king, so that they might petition the distant ruler as though he were nearby, with all the eagerness of their nature.
The craftsman's skill encouraged even someone who did not know him to worship one who was just like himself.
For the one engaged in the work, wishing to please him, pushed his skill to produce superior beauty for him.
And all the crowds rushed because of the beauty of the workmanship, making an object of worship of the one whom they had honored as a human being only a little earlier.
This became a source of ruin in human life: people were subjected to servitude because of beauty and power. You gave names to stones and wood, things that had no share in it.
It was not enough for you that you did not know God; you also waged war to give evil the name of ignorance.
You worshiped them, killed your children, performed secret rites, and acted foolishly through other arrangements of worldly affairs.
Because of them, neither your way of life nor your feasts were pure or kept under restraint. One person treacherously killed his companion, harmed him through deceit, and harmed his fellow craftsman.
For everything was mixed together: bloodshed, murder, theft, treachery, wrongdoing, lack of faithfulness, disorder, and false oaths. All these things bring distress to those who practice them.
They forget kindness, defile souls, exchange newborn children, and hold their feasts without order, with adultery and impurity.
For the practices associated with their idols, whose names have perished, and their worship are the beginning of all evil.

It is also a cause of destruction: when they enjoy themselves, they become defiled; when they prophesy, they lie; while they live, they act unjustly; and when they swear falsely, they do not withdraw it.
They trust in idols that have no usefulness, swear wicked oaths, and do not expect any punishment to come from them.
Two things will certainly come upon them, because they thought wickedly about God and turned their attention to idols, and because they swore deceitfully by worthless things and despised the truth.
This is not the power of retribution because of oaths, but punishment for the sin of sinners and condemnation of the unjust for what they have done.
But you, our God, are kind and forgiving. You are patient, your goodness is great, and you sustain everyone.
Even if we sin, we are yours, for we know your power. Yet we do not sin, because we know that we are counted as yours.
To know you is complete righteousness, and to know your truth is the root of immortality.
The work of human hands has not led us astray: their vanity, the shadow of their paintings, the fruitless labor of their hands, empty visions and changing images.
It is beloved in the eyes of fools, who desire dead things—a splendor with no breath in it.
They are evildoers and deserve this very hope, those who struggle over them, love them, and worship them.

For look: a potter laboriously treads soft clay and molds vessels from it for use. From the same clay he makes vessels that are clean for service and vessels that are unclean for their work. The potter himself assigns each one to its use.

With wicked craftsmanship he molds from it a god for a futile purpose, though he himself was brought out of the earth a short time before. Soon he returns to the earth, and the debt of his soul is demanded of him.

He is anxious that he cannot work, not because his life is short or long, but about a wasted life of gold, silver, and bronze [?]. They imitate him, fashion him in uncleanness, and set him up in glory.
His heart is ashes, his hope is dust, and his life is dishonorable clay.
For he does not know the one who formed him, placed a complete soul within him, and breathed the spirit of life into him.
They considered the span of their lives a joke, and their life like a merchant’s buying and selling, with all his profit coming through wrongdoing.
He knows better than anyone that he is sinning—the one who makes carved images from earthy material and serves them.
They are all contemptible and miserable, and the enemies of your people exert their power over the life of the little one [?].

For they considered all the idols of the nations gods, though their eyes do not see [?], their noses do not smell the air, their ears do not hear, the fingers of their hands do not move, and their feet are unable to walk.
For a human being made them, and a spirit of falsehood fashioned them. None of them can make a god like a human being.
He is a mortal human being and makes dead things with sinful hands. He is better than what he worships, because he can live, but they cannot.
In their foolishness they even worship unclean animals, and these are worse than those.
For they longed for the appearance of animals, to accept them as good things, and they departed from the praise of God and from his blessing.
For this reason he took vengeance on them as they deserved, for they were scourged with every creeping and crawling creature.
You did many good things for your people and brought them unfamiliar food to satisfy their desire. You brought them a brood of quail to satisfy their desire.

They craved food, and you sent it to them, and they turned back in their desires. They asked for little, made use of food they had not known, and were strengthened. You withheld from them nothing they needed.
To those you sent famine and poverty because of their grumbling and their tyranny, while to these you showed that you had scourged their enemies.
You brought the venom of snakes upon them, and snakes bit them for their wrongdoing, but the wrath was not meant to destroy them.
Rather, they were disciplined briefly for correction, so that they would remember life through the commandment of your law.
For the one who turned back was not kept alive because he saw power, but because of you, for you are the giver of life to all.
And through these things you convinced our enemies that you are the one who saves from every evil.
For locusts and flies bit them, and they died, and there was no remedy to save their lives, because they deserved to have vengeance taken on them through these creatures.
But your children overcame the terror of serpents and their jaws, because you sent your grace and healed them.
And so that they would remember your words, you rescued them and quickly gave them relief, so that they would not fall into the depths and forget you, since they were worthy of your blessings.
For neither roots nor poultices healed them, but your word, Lord, which heals everyone.
For you have authority over death and life. You bring people down to the gates of Sheol and bring them up.
For a person is killed by his wickedness, and the spirit departs and does not return, nor does the soul that is taken away come back.
And no one can escape from your hands.
For you scourged the wicked who denied you with the strength of your arm. You changed their rain into hailstones and pursued them with no one to rescue them, and you destroyed them with fire.
And in your great glory the waters did not extinguish it. This was the marvel: in water, which extinguishes fire, the fire blazed all the more, because all creation helps the righteous in battle.
And when you wish, fire obeys and does not burn the animals you sent against the wicked, who, when they saw this, believed that they were being judged by God's judgment.
And when you wished, fire burned in water and blazed up to burn the crops of the oppressors' land.
And you fed your people with the food of angels and gave them bread from heaven, prepared without toil, sweeter than every sweetness and more flavorful than every flavor.
With the things you prepared, you openly gave sweetness to your children and served them according to their desires; it was blended for each person according to his wish.

Fire remained amid snow and ice, and they did not melt, so that they might know that fire destroyed their enemies' crops as it blazed within the hail, and that you sent lightning amid hailstones and rain.
So that the righteous might be set apart and not forget your power.
For all your creation is subject to you, and you assigned punishment to oppressors and gave health to those who trust in you.
For this reason it changes in every way and serves your gift, which provides for each person according to his wishes.
To teach the children whom the Lord loves that it is not the production of crops that sustains a human being, but your word that preserves those who believe in it.
Many times fire came, and they were not harmed; and those things that did not melt from fire melted before the sun when it came in its heat.
So that they might know that even the sun stands in thanksgiving and offers it to you as its light dawns.
For the hope of the wicked melts like winter ice and is poured out like water that is thrown away.
For your judgments are great and astonishing to recount. Therefore those who are shameless in their souls have gone astray.
For sinners thought they could enslave your holy people; they reckoned themselves prisoners of darkness and counselors of the night.
They hoped to escape the thoughts of the world and hoped to hide their sins. For what they had done they were rebuked and scattered; they were terribly frightened, shaken, and thrown down.
And the darkness that seized them imprisoned them in fear, and a sound of cursing met them. Suddenly their eyes grew dark, and there was no light upon them.
They were scattered by a rush of fire, and their flame was bright and did not go out. They thought they would have light in the darkness of that night.
The fire alone gave them light, but they could not see its appearance. The sight they saw was terrible.
They intended to practice the craft of sorcerers, but in their proud thinking they were afflicted with humiliation, [?], and terror.
Their souls were treated harshly, and they grew sick with ridicule and fear.
Every strange thing frightened them: flies in their filth and creeping things in [?]. And they fell because of birds.
They trembled and perished, and they fled from air that was nothing—unbelievers who would not believe.
For their wickedness testifies against them and condemns them for doing evil, and they clung to their own thoughts.
What is their fear but the betrayal of evil and the helper of the thoughts within it?
It expects something less than itself, yet it is greater than what it does not know, and it is the cause of the distress that comes.
The night was powerless and could not come from Sheol in its chains; in it they lay asleep.
In your sleep you saw your own soul, which you were guiding, and you blew upon everything you saw.
You appeared to be bound, though not with bonds, and you were imprisoned.
Whether you were a laborer or a shepherd, or were worn out by work in the fields, you were seized and subjected to an ordeal you had not expected.

There is one entrance to the darkness, and everyone prays because of it. For they were all bound by a single chain of darkness—whether it was whistling winds, or the sound of the wings of birds uttering sweet calls, or the sound of water rushing violently,

or the sound of stones falling upon stones, or the sound of animals running and leaping unseen, or the sound of wild beasts roaring, or the sound of an echo from among the mountains—it left them gripped by fear.
For all creatures shine in the beauty of the light, and all his work is undisturbed.
Only over them was there a heavy night, an image of the darkness that was to come upon them. It was a heavy night for them.
But for your righteous people there was a great, brilliant light. They heard his voice but did not see his form, and they too were scourged and blessed.
For they admitted that they were being rightly punished, because they had been the first to oppress, and they pleaded with him.
A pillar of fire showed them the way, and you gave them honor from the heat of the sun.

Their enemies were deprived of light and imprisoned in darkness because they had kept many of your children in bondage. Through them the light of the law was to shine, given without corruption to the people of their enemies.

They planned to kill the infants and the holy ones, but one holy child was preserved to rebuke them, bringing destruction upon many of their children. And you destroyed the enemies of your people all together with mighty waters.
That night was known to our fathers, so that they might know with certainty in whom they had trusted for life.
You gave life to your people, the righteous, and destruction to their enemies.
You took vengeance on the enemies, and you called us, sanctified us, and glorified us.

For your faithful servants ministered secretly through your grace, and laws of truth were established together, so that the holy ones might receive together what is good and what is right, and from this hour offer praise to the Father.
Unmatched distress came upon the enemies, and they mourned over the destruction of their children.
In that judgment, retribution was exacted from slave and master alike, and king and poor person suffered equally.
All of them together died the same death, and they could not be counted. The living could not bury the dead, for in the blink of an eye their precious offspring had been destroyed.
They had not believed any of these things because of their sorcery, but when their firstborn perished, they acknowledged that the people were God's son.
For stillness and silence held everything, and at midnight there was bewilderment.
Your almighty word came from heaven, from the throne of the kingdom, a wonder to warriors, and swept over the earth amid destruction.
It brought a sharp sword at your command, which shows no partiality. It stood and fulfilled everything according to the command; it reached to heaven and stood upon the earth.
Then suddenly visions of evil dreams troubled them, and a fear they had not expected came upon them.
They were being thrown down and falling here and there. Each of them, between death and life, told the others what offense they were dying for.
For the dreams that terrified them had told them this beforehand, so that they would not perish without knowing why they were suffering so terribly.
But at one time a trial of death also reached the righteous, and many perished in the wilderness. Yet your wrath did not continue to the end.

For a righteous man hurried and put on the priestly garments. He advanced to fight with the weapons of his priesthood: petition and prayer. He offered incense for atonement, stood against the fury, and turned back the wrath. The plague was stopped, and he was recognized as your servant.
He overcame the multitude, not by bodily strength or by a lifetime of toil, but by a word he subdued the destroyer, recalling the covenants and the oaths of the ancestors.
For when the dead had fallen in heaps upon one another, he stood between the dead and the living, turned back the wrath, and cut a path between the dead and the living.
On the [?] of his garment was the whole people, and the glory of the ancestors was engraved on the four rows of stones upon his shoulders. The crown of your majesty was upon his head.
The destroyer obeyed these things, but they were afraid, for the trial of wrath alone was enough.
But merciless fury remained upon the wicked to the very end, for they already knew beforehand what awaited them.
For they turned back so that they would be no more. They had sent them away hurriedly, but then regretted it and pursued them.
For mourning was upon their hands, and they were rushing to bury the dead, yet they conceived another senseless plan. Those whom they had sent out while pleading with them, they pursued as fugitives.

For retribution was drawing them toward an unavoidable end, and they did not remember what had happened to them, so that through torment they might complete this one punishment still missing from their scourges.
Your people would experience an extraordinary journey, while they would meet an unfamiliar death.
For the whole creation, in the order of its nature, was being created anew, submitting in its nature to your commands, so that your servants might be kept unharmed.

A cloud overshadowed the whole camp, and dry land appeared from the depths of the earth out of the standing waters. An unobstructed road was opened through the Red Sea, and a plain full of every kind of grass met them out of the surging waves.
Through it the whole people passed, sheltered by your hand, and they saw wonders and marvels.
They grazed like horses and skipped like lambs, and they praised you, Lord, who had delivered them.

For they remembered what had happened during their stay in a foreign land: how, instead of animals being born, the earth brought forth creeping and swarming creatures, and instead of creatures moving in the water, the river poured out many frogs.
And after these things, at last they again saw a new birth of birds, when your people, who had longed for food before, asked for food to sustain them.
And, as though to comfort them, you brought quails up from the sea for them.
Scourges came upon sinners; wrath and distress did not occur without prior signs. For they justly suffered for their wicked deeds, since they had devised an evil course.
Those did not welcome people they did not know when they were there, while these enslaved the foreigners who provided for them.
And not only this, but judgment will come upon them because they were unwilling to release the foreigners.
But those welcomed with joy the people on whose account they received retribution, because they mistreated them with exhausting labor.

They were struck with darkness, like the people of Sodom at the righteous man's door, who were struck with dazzling flashes and with the darkness that covered them. Each of them was searching for the entrance to his door.

For their sake the elements are arranged, just as on a harp, in the sound of melodies, the names of the notes change, yet the sound remains throughout. This is an illustration showing the forms of the things that truly happened.
For barren land was being turned into pools, and creeping creatures were walking on the land.
And fire was blazing in water, yet it did not burn with its strength, and the water, with its strength, did not extinguish the fire.
And the flame did not burn the destructive animals or harm their flesh as they walked through it, nor did the hailstones that destroy fruit melt.
For in everything, Lord, you exalted your people and glorified them. You did not abandon them in anything, but helped them everywhere and at all times.
